'''Bruno Correa Fernandes Caboclo''' (born September 21, 1995) is a Brazilian professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Dubai Basketball]] of the [[ABA League]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. He plays at the [[power forward]] and [[center (basketball)|center]] positions. After making his debut for [[Esporte Clube Pinheiros (basketball)|Pinheiros]] in Brazil, Caboclo was drafted 20th overall by the [[Toronto Raptors]] in the [[2014 NBA draft]], and spent seven seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).

==Early life==
Born in [[Osasco]],<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.tsn.ca/nba/player-bio/bruno-caboclo/bio | title=Bruno Caboclo Stats, News, Video, Bio, Highlights on TSN }}</ref> Caboclo was raised in [[Barueri]] and [[Pirapora do Bom Jesus]] in the state of [[São Paulo (state)|São Paulo]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.esporte.gov.br/index.php/fique-por-dentro/67-lista-fique-por-dentro/48071-destaque-da-ldb-bruno-caboclo-e-selecionado-por-equipe-da-nba |title=Destaque da LDB, Bruno Caboclo é selecionado por equipe da NBA |work=Esporte.gov.br |date=June 27, 2014 |access-date=January 8, 2015|language=pt}}</ref> At age 13, he began playing basketball for [[Grêmio Barueri Futebol|Grêmio Recreativo Barueri]], a social club that invites children from local public schools to play sports.<ref name=cbs>{{cite web|first=James|last=Herbert|url=http://www.cbssports.com/nba/eye-on-basketball/24606082/how-bruno-caboclo-got-here|title=How Bruno Caboclo got here|work=CBSSports.com|date=July 3, 2014|access-date=July 10, 2014}}</ref>

In January 2013, Caboclo linked up with coach Rafael Franco at Score Academy in [[Raleigh, North Carolina]]. In his first game, against top-five-ranked junior college [[Vincennes University]], the {{Height|ft=6|in=9}} forward with an almost {{Height|ft=7|in=7}} wingspan missed three-pointer after three-pointer. Coach Franco told Caboclo he had to be aggressive and had to rebound, and the scoring would come, and was temporarily banned from shooting threes.<ref name="cbs" />

==Professional career==

===Pinheiros (2013–2014)===
In April 2013, Caboclo returned to Brazil and signed with [[Esporte Clube Pinheiros (basketball)|Pinheiros]] of the [[Novo Basquete Brasil]] (NBB).<ref name="cbs" /> In 2013–14, he played 17 games, averaging 4.8 points and 3.1 rebounds per game.

===Toronto Raptors (2014–2018)===
On June 26, 2014, Caboclo was selected with the 20th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Toronto Raptors]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Ethan|last=Rothstein|url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2014/6/26/5847824/nba-draft-results-2014-raptors-bruno-caboclo|title=Raptors select Bruno Caboclo with 20th pick in 2014 NBA Draft|work=SBNation.com|date=June 26, 2014|access-date=June 26, 2014}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|first=Joseph|last=Zucker|url=http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2111355-bruno-caboclo-to-toronto-raptors-latest-news-reaction-and-analysis|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140630051128/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/2111355-bruno-caboclo-to-toronto-raptors-latest-news-reaction-and-analysis|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 30, 2014|title=Bruno Caboclo to Toronto Raptors: Latest News, Reaction and Analysis|work=BleacherReport.com|date=June 26, 2014|access-date=June 26, 2014}}</ref> During draft night, it was infamously reported by [[Fran Fraschilla]] during Caboclo's selection that he was "two years away from being two years away."<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://hashtagbasketball.com/toronto-raptors/content/bruno-caboclo-still-2-years-from-being-2-years-away|title = Bruno Caboclo is Still 2 Years Away from Being 2 Years Away | Toronto Raptors}}</ref> On July 9, he signed with the Raptors and joined them for the [[2014 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/caboclo_signs070914|title=Raptors Sign First-Round Pick Bruno Caboclo|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2014|access-date=July 9, 2014}}</ref> On November 21, Caboclo made his NBA debut against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. In 12 minutes of action, he recorded eight points, one rebound and one block in the 124–83 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141121/MILTOR/gameinfo.html|title=Williams scores 22 as Raptors beat Bucks 124-83|work=NBA.com|date=November 21, 2014|access-date=November 21, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160317062601/http://www.nba.com/games/20141121/MILTOR/gameinfo.html|archive-date=March 17, 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> On December 25, Caboclo was assigned to the [[Fort Wayne Mad Ants]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Caboclo Assigned To Fort Wayne Mad Ants|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/press-releases/caboclo_122514|access-date=December 25, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=December 25, 2014}}</ref> He was recalled by the Raptors on January 1, 2015, after appearing in three games for the Mad Ants while averaging 4.3 points, 2.7 rebounds and 13.0 minutes per game.<ref>{{cite news|title=Raptors Recall Caboclo From Mad Ants|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/raptors-recall-caboclo-mad-ants-0|access-date=January 1, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=January 1, 2015}}</ref> Caboclo was reassigned to the Mad Ants on February 18,<ref>{{cite news|title=Raptors Reassign Caboclo To Mad Ants|url=http://www.nba.com/raptors/press-releases/caboclo_021815|access-date=February 18, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=February 18, 2015}}</ref> and recalled again on March 8.<ref>{{cite news|first=Zarar|last=Siddiqi|title=Bruno Caboclo Recalled from D-League|url=http://www.raptorsrepublic.com/2015/03/08/bruno-caboclo-recalled-from-d-league/|access-date=March 10, 2015|work=RaptorsRepublic.com|date=March 8, 2015}}</ref>

In July 2015, Caboclo re-joined the Raptors for the [[2015 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsnet.ca/basketball/nba/raptors-ready-to-double-down-on-bruno-caboclo/|title=Raptors ready to double down on Bruno Caboclo|work=Sportsnet.ca|date=July 10, 2015|access-date=July 10, 2015}}</ref> On September 29, the Raptors exercised their third-year team option on Caboclo's rookie scale contract, extending the contract through the 2016–17 season.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://basketball.realgm.com/wiretap/239365/Raptors-Exercise-16-17-Options-On-Bruno-Caboclo-Lucas-Nogueira|title=Raptors Exercise 16-17 Options On Bruno Caboclo, Lucas Nogueira|work=RealGM.com|date=September 29, 2015|access-date=September 29, 2015}}</ref> During the 2015–16 and 2016–17 seasons, he had multiple assignments with [[Raptors 905]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 6, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170322122733/http://dleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|archive-date=March 22, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|title=2016-17 NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 6, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170126075350/http://dleague.nba.com/assignments/|archive-date=January 26, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> In April 2017, Caboclo led Raptors 905 to the D-League Finals. In Game 3 of the series, Caboclo led the way with a game-high 31 points and 11 rebounds as Raptors 905 downed the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] 122–96 to take the best-of-three series 2–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/nba/bruno-caboclo-raptors-905-dleague-1.4089617|title=Bruno Caboclo leads Raptors 905 to D-League crown|work=CBC.ca|date=April 27, 2017|access-date=July 2, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://gleague.nba.com/news/2017-nba-d-league-finals-raptors-905-rio-grande-valley-vipers/|title=2017 NBA D-League Finals: Raptors 905 Defeat Rio Grande Valley Vipers, 2-1|work=NBA.com|date=April 28, 2017|access-date=July 2, 2017}}</ref>

===Sacramento Kings (2018)===
On February 8, 2018, Caboclo was traded to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for [[Malachi Richardson]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-bruno-caboclo|title=Kings Acquire Bruno Caboclo|work=NBA.com|date=February 8, 2018|access-date=February 8, 2018}}</ref> On March 23, he was assigned to the [[Stockton Kings|Reno Bighorns]],<ref>{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Jones|url=https://www.sacbee.com/sports/nba/sacramento-kings/kings-blog/article206632999.html|title=Kings assign seldom-used forward to the G League|work=SacBee.com|date=March 23, 2018|access-date=April 16, 2018}}</ref> Sacramento's [[NBA G League|G League]] affiliate and recalled two days later.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kings-bruno-caboclo-recalled-from-g-league/|title=Kings' Bruno Caboclo: Recalled from G-League|work=CBSSports.com|date=March 25, 2018|access-date=April 16, 2018}}</ref>

===Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2018–2019)===
On August 20, 2018, Caboclo signed a training camp contract with the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Rockets Sign Bruno Caboclo|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-bruno-caboclo|website=NBA.com|access-date=August 20, 2018|date=August 20, 2018}}</ref> He was waived on October 13.<ref>{{cite web|title=Rockets Waive Four Players|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-waive-four-players|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 14, 2018|date=October 13, 2018}}</ref> He was then added to the training camp roster of the Rockets’ G League affiliate, the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Rio Grande Valley Vipers Finalize Training Camp Roster|url=https://riograndevalley.gleague.nba.com/news/rio-grande-valley-vipers-finalize-training-camp-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2018|access-date=October 21, 2018|archive-date=October 22, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181022034113/https://riograndevalley.gleague.nba.com/news/rio-grande-valley-vipers-finalize-training-camp-roster/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Memphis Grizzlies (2019–2020)===
On January 24, 2019, Caboclo signed with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] on a 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Bruno Caboclo to 10-day contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-bruno-caboclo-to-10-day-contract-190124|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 24, 2019|date=January 24, 2019}}</ref> On February 3, Caboclo signed a second 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Bruno Caboclo to second 10-day contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-bruno-caboclo-to-second-10-day-contract-190203|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 13, 2019|date=February 3, 2019}}</ref> On February 13, Caboclo signed a multi-year contract with the Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite web|title=Memphis Grizzlies sign Bruno Caboclo to multi-year contract|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/memphis-grizzlies-sign-bruno-caboclo-to-multi-year-contract-190213|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 13, 2019|date=February 13, 2019}}</ref> On March 25, he recorded his first double-double and scored a career high 24 points against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards/caboclos-career-high-24-points-lead-grizzlies-past-thunder/2019/03/25/99f589da-4f72-11e9-bdb7-44f948cc0605_story.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190326121452/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards/caboclos-career-high-24-points-lead-grizzlies-past-thunder/2019/03/25/99f589da-4f72-11e9-bdb7-44f948cc0605_story.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=2019-03-26|title=Caboclo's career-high 24 points lead Grizzlies past Thunder|newspaper=Washington Post|language=en|access-date=2019-03-28}}</ref> Caboclo was assigned to the [[Memphis Hustle]] on January 13, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Grizzlies' Bruno Caboclo: Dispatched to G League |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-bruno-caboclo-dispatched-to-g-league/ |access-date=January 13, 2020 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 13, 2020}}</ref>

===Houston Rockets (2020–2021)===
On February 6, 2020, Caboclo was traded to the [[Houston Rockets]] in exchange for [[Jordan Bell]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-acquire-bruno-caboclo|title=Rockets Acquire Bruno Caboclo|work=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2020}}</ref>

On January 13, 2021, Caboclo was waived by the Rockets.<ref>{{cite news |last1=DuBose |first1=Ben |title=Rockets waiving Bruno Caboclo to clear roster spot for Harden trade|url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/2021/01/13/rockets-waiving-bruno-caboclo-to-clear-roster-spot-for-harden-trade/ |access-date=January 13, 2021 |work=Rockets Wire |date=January 13, 2021}}</ref>

===Limoges CSP (2021)===
On February 26, 2021 [[Limoges CSP]] officially announced signing Bruno Caboclo for the rest of the season.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/limoges-csp-officially-announces-bruno-caboclo/|title=Limoges CSP officially announces Bruno Caboclo|newspaper=Sportando|publisher=Sportando.com|access-date=26 February 2021}}</ref> He averaged 10 points and 5 rebounds per game.

===São Paulo FC (2021–2022)===
On August 12, 2021, Caboclo signed with [[São Paulo FC (basketball)|São Paulo FC]] of the [[Novo Basquete Brasil]] (NBB).<ref>{{cite news |title=Bruno Caboclo joins Sao Paolo |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/bruno-caboclo-joins-sao-paolo/ |website=Sportando |access-date=August 12, 2021 |date=August 12, 2021 |last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }}</ref> He won the [[2021–22 BCL Americas]] championship with São Paulo, the team's first continental title. Caboclo averaged 23.9 points and 11.1 rebounds, both second-best averages in the BCL Americas. He also led the competition in blocks per game, with 3.6, and [[efficiency (basketball)|efficiency]] with 32.8 per game.<ref>{{cite web |title=Basketball Champions League 2022 |url=http://championsleague.basketball |website=FIBA.basketball |access-date=11 April 2022 |language=en}}</ref> In the [[2022 BCL Americas Final|final]] on April 10, 2022, Caboclo had a team-high 29 points, 7 rebounds and 3 blocks. He was named the BCL Americas' season Most Valuable Player after the Tournament.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bruno Caboclo wins BCLA 2022 MVP |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/bclamericas/21-22/news/bruno-caboclo-wins-bcla-2022-mvp |access-date=11 April 2022 |work=FIBA.basketball |language=en}}</ref> Later, he was also named the MVP of the 2021–22 NBB season.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=BRUNO CABOCLO IS NAMED MVP OF THE 2021-22 NBB SEASON. CHECK OUT ALL THE AWARDS |url=https://www.streetopia.me/m/news/62ac842f9be04d64d3123cf5/bruno-caboclo-is-named-mvp-of-the-2021-22-nbb-season-check-out-all-the-awards |access-date=2022-07-17 |website=streetopia.me}}</ref>

Following his successful year in Brazil, Caboclo participated in the [[2022 NBA Summer League]] with the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{cite web |date=July 2, 2022 |title=Jazz Announce 2022 Summer League Roster |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz-announce-2022-summer-league-roster |access-date=July 5, 2022 |publisher=NBA}}</ref>

On August 26, 2022, Caboclo signed with the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Krivitsky |first=Bobby |title=Celtics Officially Sign Bruno Caboclo |url=https://www.si.com/nba/celtics/top-stories/celtics-officially-sign-bruno-caboclo |access-date=2022-09-06 |website=Sports Illustrated |date=August 26, 2022 |language=en}}</ref> He was waived on September 20.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Celtics' Bruno Caboclo: Waived by Celtics |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/celtics-bruno-caboclo-waived-by-celtics/ |access-date=September 20, 2022 |website=CBS Sports|date=September 20, 2022 }}</ref>

===Mexico City Capitanes (2022)===
On November 4, 2022, Caboclo was named to the opening night roster for the [[Mexico City Capitanes]] of the [[NBA G League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://capitanes.gleague.nba.com/roster|title=Capitanes de Ciudad de México roster 2022-23|date=November 4, 2022|access-date=November 4, 2022}}</ref> He appeared in two games for the Capitanes, averaging 12 points and 5 rebounds.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bruno Caboclo |url=https://stats.gleague.nba.com/player/203998/career/ |access-date=2023-01-05 |website=NBA G League Stats |language=en}}</ref>

===Ratiopharm Ulm (2023)===
On January 5, 2023, Caboclo signed a multi-year deal with [[Ratiopharm Ulm]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]] (BBL). He signed a contract until the end of 2024.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ulm inks Caboclo to multi-year deal {{!}} EuroCup |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/news/ulm-inks-caboclo-to-multi-year-deal/ |access-date=2023-01-05 |website=Euroleague Basketball |date=January 5, 2023 |language=en-GB}}</ref> Caboclo was a key player in Ulm' 2023 German championship-winning team,<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-06-16 |title=Ulm claims its first German League title! |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/news/ulm-claims-its-first-german-league-title/ |access-date=2023-06-17 |website=Euroleague |language=en}}</ref> averaging 14,9 points and 6.3 rebounds in Bundesliga play.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Ratiopharm Ulm |url=https://www.easycredit-bbl.de/teams/aa1d6b4a-27de-4cfd-a765-eae32dc5e83b/2022 |access-date=2023-06-17 |website=Basketball-Bundesliga}}</ref> Afterwards he activated a release clause in his contract.<ref>{{Cite web |last=sportschau.de |title=Basketball-Bundesliga: Center Caboclo verlässt BBL-Champion Ulm |url=https://www.sportschau.de/newsticker/dpa-center-caboclo-verlaesst-bbl-champion-ulm-100.html |access-date=2023-07-01 |website=Sportschau |language=de}}</ref>

===Umana Reyer Venezia (2023)===
On June 30, 2023, Caboclo put pen to paper on a contract with [[Umana Reyer Venezia]] of the Italian [[Serie A (basketball)|Serie A]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Rigo |first=Francesco |date=2023-06-30 |title=Colpo Umana Reyer: firmato Bruno Caboclo! |url=https://www.reyer.it/news/maschile/2023-06-30/colpo-umana-reyer-firmato-bruno-caboclo/ |access-date=2023-07-01 |website=Umana Reyer Venezia |language=it}}</ref>

===Partizan Belgrade (2023–2024)===
On November 7, 2023, Caboclo signed a contract with the Serbian team [[KK Partizan|Partizan Belgrade]].<ref>{{cite news |title=BRUNO CABOCLO IS THE NEW PARTIZAN MOZZART BET PLAYER |url=https://www.aba-liga.com/news/49682/bruno-caboclo-is-the-new-partizan-mozzart-bet-player/ |access-date=16 April 2024 |work=aba-liga.com |date=7 November 2023}}</ref> Over the 2023–24 season, Caboclo averaged 9.4 points and 4 rebounds on 63.7% shooting from the field in 27 EuroLeague games for Partizan. In June 2024, Caboclo left the club for private reasons without the club's approval in the midst of the [[Basketball League of Serbia|Serbian League]] playoffs series. The club's president later said that despite that, Caboclo will stay with the team for the next season as well.<ref>{{cite news |title=Ostoja potvrdio: "Kaboklo ostaje u Partizanu, ali..." |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/euroleague/29360/ostoja-potvrdio-kaboklo-ostaje-u-partizanu-ali/vest |access-date=11 June 2024 |work=b92.net |date=7 June 2024 |language=Serbian}}</ref> The season was deemed to be unsuccessful for Partizan as they finished the season without lifting any trophy.<ref>{{cite news |title=Očekuje nas burno leto u Partizanu – ko ostaje, a ko odlazi? |url=https://www.b92.net/sport/kosarka/srpska-kosarka/28999/ocekuje-nas-burno-leto-u-partizanu-ko-ostaje-a-ko-odlazi/vest |access-date=11 June 2024 |date=6 June 2024 |language=Serbian}}</ref>

===Hapoel Shlomo Tel Aviv (2024–2026)===
On August 30, 2024, Caboclo signed with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Bruno Caboclo makes his way to Hapoel Tel Aviv, joins Johnathan Motley |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/eurocup/1710906/bruno-caboclo-hapoel-tel-aviv-bkt-eurocup-2024-2025/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=30 August 2024 |language=en |date=30 August 2024}}</ref>

On October 9, 2025, it was announced that Caboclo would miss multiple months after undergoing surgery to repair a [[disc herniation|herniated disc]] in his back.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Hapoel: Bruno Caboclo undergoes back surgery|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/euroleague/news/hapoel-bruno-caboclo-undergoes-back-surgery/|access-date=December 21, 2025|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|language=en}}</ref>

===Dubai Basketball (2026)===
On January 15, 2026, Caboclo left Hapoel and signed with [[Dubai Basketball]] of the [[ABA League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dubai reels in Bruno Caboclo
|url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/en/euroleague/news/dubai-basketball-reels-in-bruno-caboclo/|access-date=January 15, 2026|website=euroleaguebasketball.net|language=en}}</ref>

==National team career==
Caboclo has been a member of the senior [[Brazilian national basketball team]]. With Brazil, he played at the [[2017 FIBA AmeriCup]]<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20181123154218/http://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/p/rpp//q/Bruno%20Caboclo/pid//_//players.html Bruno CABOCLO (BRA).]</ref> At the [[2019 FIBA Basketball World Cup]] and [[2023 FIBA Basketball World Cup]].

Caboclo also played with Brazil at the [[Basketball at the 2024 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2024 Olympics]] in [[Paris]]. In their third group game, he scored 33 points, on 13-for-19 shooting, and grabbed 17 rebounds against [[Japan men's national basketball team|Japan]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2024-08-02 |title=Caboclo's unforgettable masterpiece: A historic performance |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/events/mens-olympic-basketball-tournament-paris-2024/news/caboclos-unforgettable-masterpiece-a-historic-performance |access-date=2024-08-03 |website=www.fiba.basketball |language=en}}</ref> He became the first player to have more than 30 points and 15 rebounds in an Olympic game since [[Clifford Luyk]] in [[Basketball at the 1972 Summer Olympics|1972]].<ref name=":1" /> His [[Efficiency (basketball)|efficiency]] of 43 was the second highest since counting began in 2016, only trailing [[Luka Dončić]]' 49 in [[Basketball at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2020]].<ref name=":1" />
